problem: Whether the normalized Turán deficit of a Poisson–binomial pmf at its first-descent index D admits a universal variance-scaled lower bound κ/V (for V ≥ 1), independent of the number of summands and the success probabilities.
debate: Quantitative log-concavity (Turán-type) lower bounds for Bernoulli sums, in the line of Newton, Pitman, Dümbgen–Wellner, Hillion–Johnson and Johnson (ultra-log-concavity and related bounds), together with mode-location and maximal-mass results (Darroch, Bobkov–Marsiglietti–Melbourne); there is no named controversy, only a cluster of bounds.
gap: The known lower bounds on δ_k depend on n, on the success probabilities, or on k alone, and the paper says all four degenerate near the mode when summands with p_i near 0 and near 1 accumulate at fixed variance, but the supporting discussion is deferred to a later section beyond the opening.
contribution: It proves V·δ_D ≥ 1/4, shows via a binomial family that no constant above 1/3 works, derives δ_k ≥ 1/(4V+|k−D|) and 1/(4V+1) ≤ δ_c < 2/V at the rightmost mode, and illustrates the gain over ultra-log-concavity with the Haar-unitary half-circle count (1/log N versus 1/N), using a computer-assisted exact-arithmetic step.
note: The statement is clean and the constants are explicit, but you never say who needs a variance-scaled bound at the first descent index (the Haar unitary example is the only motivation offered), the 1/4 versus 1/3 gap stays open, and the computer-assisted step needs to be easy for a referee to check.
